text: You've just finished a pleasant meal. Server was great. All good, right? You simply want to wrap up, feeling satisfied.
Then the check arrives. A blank line awaits. You know you *should* tip, but why does it feel more like an obligation?
You thought tipping was for *exceptional* service, a bonus for going above and beyond. But this feels like paying for basic service already received.
Here's the invisible system: many businesses pay servers a lower base wage, relying on tips. Your contribution isn't a bonus; it's a fundamental part of their income.
The illusion breaks. You thought you were rewarding effort, but you're subsidizing labor costs. This 'choice' is a necessity, shifted onto you.
So next time you sign that check, you'll still tip. But now you see the hidden mechanism. You're participating in a system shaping how people earn a living.
